standard_prerequisites.name: The short exact sequence associated to a dense open subscheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the short exact sequence 0 -> j_!j^{-1}F -> F -> i_*i^{-1}F -> 0 for the inclusion j of a dense open with closed complement i
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exact sequence whose long exact cohomology sequence drives the comparison.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the higher direct images of a finite morphism and the Leray spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the vanishing of R^q i_* for the finite closed immersion i : Z -> X and the Leray spectral sequence, whose combination gives H^q(X, i_*i^{-1}F) = H^q(Z, i^*F)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of the cohomology of the third term with the cohomology of the zero-dimensional set Z.

standard_prerequisites.name: The dimension zero structure of the complement
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the standing situation in which the complement of a dense open in the curve is a finite set of k-rational points
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that Z is a disjoint union of spectra of algebraically closed fields, hence has no higher cohomology.

core_obligations: Identify the complement (proof lines 15500-15503): density of X' makes Z = X minus X' zero-dimensional, hence a finite set of k-rational points.

Use the short exact sequence (proof lines 15504-15507): the sequence 0 -> j_!j^{-1}F -> F -> i_*i^{-1}F -> 0 gives a long exact sequence linking the cohomology of F and of j_!j^{-1}F, so the two sets of statements differ exactly by the contribution of i_*i^{-1}F.

Identify the remaining term (proof lines 15508-15516): since the closed immersion i is finite, its higher direct images vanish, and the Leray spectral sequence gives H^q(X, i_*i^{-1}F) = H^q(Z, i^*F); because Z is a disjoint union of spectra of algebraically closed fields, this group vanishes for q > 0.

Conclude the equivalence (proof lines 15517-15545): with the third term contributing only in degree zero, the five-lemma style comparison along the long exact sequence shows that the statements (vanishing) through (surjective) hold for F if and only if they hold for j_!j^{-1}F, using constructibility where the statement requires it.
proof_roadmap: Observe that the complement of the dense open is a finite set of rational points.
Write F as an extension of i_*i^{-1}F by j_!j^{-1}F and compare the two long exact cohomology sequences.
Kill the contribution of the closed complement using finiteness of i and the vanishing of cohomology on a disjoint union of algebraically closed fields.
difficulty_reason: The lemma transfers the vanishing and surjectivity statements of the standing situation from a constructible sheaf F to its extension by zero from a dense open, and back (statement lines 15490-15497). The proof (proof lines 15499-15545) uses the short exact sequence attached to the dense open, identifies the cohomology of the quotient term i_*i^{-1}F with the cohomology of the zero-dimensional complement via finiteness of the closed immersion and the Leray spectral sequence, and observes that the complement, a disjoint union of spectra of algebraically closed fields, has no higher cohomology, so the comparison along the long exact sequence is an equivalence. H2: one exact sequence comparison with two identifications, written out.
